name: ci

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches:
    - main

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  WEAVER_VERSION: 0.26.1
  YAMLLINT_VERSION: 1.37.0

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - name: self-checkout
      uses: actions/checkout@v7
    - name: yamllint-install
      run: pipx install "yamllint==${YAMLLINT_VERSION}"
    - name: weaver-install
      run: |
        cd "${RUNNER_TEMP}"
        archive="weaver-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz"
        base="https://github.com/open-telemetry/weaver/releases/download/v${WEAVER_VERSION}"
        curl -fsSLO "${base}/${archive}"
        curl -fsSLO "${base}/${archive}.sha256"
        sha256sum -c "${archive}.sha256"
        tar -xJf "${archive}"
        sudo install "weaver-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/weaver" /usr/local/bin/weaver
        weaver --version
    - name: yaml-lint
      run: make yaml-lint
    - name: weaver-check
      run: make weaver-check
  docs:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - name: self-checkout
      uses: actions/checkout@v7
    - name: weaver-install
      run: |
        cd "${RUNNER_TEMP}"
        archive="weaver-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz"
        base="https://github.com/open-telemetry/weaver/releases/download/v${WEAVER_VERSION}"
        curl -fsSLO "${base}/${archive}"
        curl -fsSLO "${base}/${archive}.sha256"
        sha256sum -c "${archive}.sha256"
        tar -xJf "${archive}"
        sudo install "weaver-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/weaver" /usr/local/bin/weaver
        weaver --version
    - name: weaver-docs
      run: |
        make weaver-docs
        git add --intent-to-add docs
        if ! git diff --exit-code -- docs; then
          echo "::error::docs/ is out of date. Run 'make weaver-docs' and commit the result."
          exit 1
        fi

# SigNoz Semantic Conventions

## 🏷️ Attributes

### [`audit`](audit.md)

- [`signoz.audit.action_category`](audit.md#signoz-audit-action-category): Category of the audited operation.
- [`signoz.audit.outcome`](audit.md#signoz-audit-outcome): Outcome of the audited operation.
- [`signoz.audit.verb`](audit.md#signoz-audit-verb): Operation the principal performed on the resource.

### [`genai`](genai.md)

- [`signoz.gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens.cost`](genai.md#signoz-gen-ai-usage-cache-read-input-tokens-cost): The monetary cost of the input tokens served from a provider-managed cache.
- [`signoz.gen_ai.usage.cache_write.input_tokens.cost`](genai.md#signoz-gen-ai-usage-cache-write-input-tokens-cost): The monetary cost of the input tokens written to a provider-managed cache.
- [`signoz.gen_ai.usage.input_tokens.cost`](genai.md#signoz-gen-ai-usage-input-tokens-cost): The monetary cost of the input tokens billed at the model's standard input rate.
- [`signoz.gen_ai.usage.output_tokens.cost`](genai.md#signoz-gen-ai-usage-output-tokens-cost): The monetary cost of the output tokens a model generated.
- [`signoz.gen_ai.usage.tokens.cost`](genai.md#signoz-gen-ai-usage-tokens-cost): The total monetary cost of the tokens a model call used.

### [`identity`](identity.md)

- [`signoz.organization.id`](identity.md#signoz-organization-id): Unique identifier of the organization.
- [`signoz.principal.email`](identity.md#signoz-principal-email): Email address of the principal.
- [`signoz.principal.id`](identity.md#signoz-principal-id): Unique identifier of the principal.
- [`signoz.principal.type`](identity.md#signoz-principal-type): Kind of the principal.

### [`meter`](meter.md)

- [`connector_id`](meter.md#connector-id): The identifier of the meter connector instance that produced the metric.
- [`signoz.io/workload`](meter.md#signoz-io-workload): The SigNoz workload a Kubernetes node is dedicated to.

### [`resource`](resource.md)

- [`signoz.resource.id`](resource.md#signoz-resource-id): Unique identifier of the resource.
- [`signoz.resource.kind`](resource.md#signoz-resource-kind): Kind of the resource.
- [`signoz.resource.object`](resource.md#signoz-resource-object): Object reference of the resource in the authorization model.
- [`signoz.resource.target.id`](resource.md#signoz-resource-target-id): Unique identifier of the counterpart resource in a relation.
- [`signoz.resource.target.kind`](resource.md#signoz-resource-target-kind): Kind of the counterpart resource in a relation.
- [`signoz.resource.target.object`](resource.md#signoz-resource-target-object): Object reference of the counterpart resource in a relation.

### [`spanmetrics`](spanmetrics.md)

- [`address`](spanmetrics.md#address): The remote endpoint of an external call.
- [`operation`](spanmetrics.md#operation): The name of the aggregated spans.
- [`resource_deployment.environment`](spanmetrics.md#resource-deployment-environment): The value of `deployment.environment` on the span's Resource.
- [`resource_service.namespace`](spanmetrics.md#resource-service-namespace): The value of `service.namespace` on the span's Resource.
- [`resource_signoz.collector.id`](spanmetrics.md#resource-signoz-collector-id): A copy of `signoz.collector.id`.
- [`signoz.collector.id`](spanmetrics.md#signoz-collector-id): The identifier of the collector instance that produced the metric.
- [`span.kind`](spanmetrics.md#span-kind): The kind of the aggregated spans.
- [`status.code`](spanmetrics.md#status-code): The status code of the aggregated spans.

### [`workspace`](workspace.md)

- [`signoz.workspace.key.id`](workspace.md#signoz-workspace-key-id): Identifier of the key that authenticated the telemetry.
- [`signoz.workspace.name`](workspace.md#signoz-workspace-name): Identifier of the workspace under which the telemetry was ingested.

## 📈 Metrics

### [`meter`](meter.md)

- [`signoz.meter.cpu.node.allocatable.usage`](meter.md#signoz-meter-cpu-node-allocatable-usage): The amount of CPU allocatable on a Kubernetes node that runs SigNoz.
- [`signoz.meter.log.count`](meter.md#signoz-meter-log-count): The number of log records observed.
- [`signoz.meter.log.size`](meter.md#signoz-meter-log-size): The size of log records observed.
- [`signoz.meter.metric.datapoint.count`](meter.md#signoz-meter-metric-datapoint-count): The number of metric data points observed.
- [`signoz.meter.metric.datapoint.size`](meter.md#signoz-meter-metric-datapoint-size): The size of metric data points observed.
- [`signoz.meter.span.count`](meter.md#signoz-meter-span-count): The number of spans observed.
- [`signoz.meter.span.size`](meter.md#signoz-meter-span-size): The size of spans observed.

### [`spanmetrics`](spanmetrics.md)

- [`signoz_calls_total`](spanmetrics.md#signoz-calls-total): The number of spans observed.
- [`signoz_db_latency_count`](spanmetrics.md#signoz-db-latency-count): The number of database calls observed.
- [`signoz_db_latency_sum`](spanmetrics.md#signoz-db-latency-sum): The total duration of database calls observed.
- [`signoz_external_call_latency_count`](spanmetrics.md#signoz-external-call-latency-count): The number of external calls observed.
- [`signoz_external_call_latency_sum`](spanmetrics.md#signoz-external-call-latency-sum): The total duration of external calls observed.
- [`signoz_latency`](spanmetrics.md#signoz-latency): The duration of spans observed.

## ⚡ Events

### [`audit`](audit.md)

- [`signoz.audit.attach`](audit.md#signoz-audit-attach): Records the attachment of one SigNoz resource to another.
- [`signoz.audit.create`](audit.md#signoz-audit-create): Records the creation of a SigNoz resource.
- [`signoz.audit.delete`](audit.md#signoz-audit-delete): Records the deletion of a SigNoz resource.
- [`signoz.audit.detach`](audit.md#signoz-audit-detach): Records the detachment of one SigNoz resource from another.
- [`signoz.audit.update`](audit.md#signoz-audit-update): Records the modification of a SigNoz resource.

## 🧩 Entities

### [`identity`](identity.md)

- [`signoz.organization`](identity.md#signoz-organization): A SigNoz organization, the logical grouping of everything one SigNoz account holds.
- [`signoz.principal`](identity.md#signoz-principal): A principal of the SigNoz platform: an authenticated user or service account.

### [`resource`](resource.md)

- [`signoz.resource`](resource.md#signoz-resource): A SigNoz platform resource: an object the platform manages, such as a dashboard, an alert rule or an ingestion key.

### [`workspace`](workspace.md)

- [`signoz.workspace`](workspace.md#signoz-workspace): A SigNoz workspace.
- [`signoz.workspace.key`](workspace.md#signoz-workspace-key): A key of a SigNoz workspace.

name: prereleaser

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "The version to release, without the v prefix (e.g. 0.0.1-rc.1)"
        type: string
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  prepare:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - name: github-token-gen
      id: token
      uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
      with:
        app-id: ${{ secrets.PRIMUS_APP_ID }}
        private-key: ${{ secrets.PRIMUS_PRIVATE_KEY }}
    - name: self-checkout
      uses: actions/checkout@v7
      with:
        ref: main
        token: ${{ steps.token.outputs.token }}
    - name: release-prepare
      env:
        VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
      run: hack/release.sh prepare "${VERSION}"
    - name: git-configure
      run: |
        git config --global user.name "primus-bot[bot]"
        git config --global user.email "171087277+primus-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
    - name: release-pr
      env:
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.token.outputs.token }}
        VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
      run: |
        branch="chore/release-v${VERSION}"
        git switch -c "${branch}"
        git commit -am "chore(release): v${VERSION}"
        git push origin "${branch}"
        gh pr create --base main --head "${branch}" --title "chore(release): v${VERSION}" \
          --body "$(printf '%s\n\n%s\n' '#### Chores' "- release \`v${VERSION}\`: set \`schema_url\` in \`model/manifest.yaml\` to \`${VERSION}\`")"

name: postreleaser

on:
  release:
    types:
    - published

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  bump:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - name: github-token-gen
      id: token
      uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
      with:
        app-id: ${{ secrets.PRIMUS_APP_ID }}
        private-key: ${{ secrets.PRIMUS_PRIVATE_KEY }}
    - name: self-checkout
      uses: actions/checkout@v7
      with:
        ref: main
        token: ${{ steps.token.outputs.token }}
    - name: release-bump
      id: bump
      env:
        TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
      run: |
        next="$(hack/release.sh bump "${TAG}")"
        echo "version=${next}" >>"${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
    - name: git-configure
      if: steps.bump.outputs.version != ''
      run: |
        git config --global user.name "primus-bot[bot]"
        git config --global user.email "171087277+primus-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
    - name: postrelease-pr
      if: steps.bump.outputs.version != ''
      env:
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.token.outputs.token }}
        TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
        NEXT: ${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }}
      run: |
        if git diff --quiet; then
          echo "schema_url is already ${NEXT}."
          exit 0
        fi
        branch="chore/post-release-${TAG}"
        git switch -c "${branch}"
        git commit -am "chore(release): start ${NEXT}"
        git push origin "${branch}"
        gh pr create --base main --head "${branch}" --title "chore(release): start ${NEXT}" \
          --body "$(printf '%s\n\n%s\n' '#### Chores' "- after \`${TAG}\`, set \`schema_url\` in \`model/manifest.yaml\` to \`${NEXT}\`")"

name: releaser

on:
  release:
    types:
    - published
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tag:
        description: "The published release to attach the registry to (e.g. v0.0.1-rc.1)"
        type: string
        required: true

permissions:
  contents: write

env:
  WEAVER_VERSION: 0.26.1
  TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name || inputs.tag }}

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - name: self-checkout
      uses: actions/checkout@v7
      with:
        ref: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name || inputs.tag }}
    - name: release-verify
      run: hack/release.sh verify "${TAG}"
    - name: weaver-install
      run: |
        cd "${RUNNER_TEMP}"
        archive="weaver-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.xz"
        base="https://github.com/open-telemetry/weaver/releases/download/v${WEAVER_VERSION}"
        curl -fsSLO "${base}/${archive}"
        curl -fsSLO "${base}/${archive}.sha256"
        sha256sum -c "${archive}.sha256"
        tar -xJf "${archive}"
        sudo install "weaver-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/weaver" /usr/local/bin/weaver
        weaver --version
    - name: release-package
      run: hack/release.sh package "${TAG}" dist
    - name: github-release-upload
      env:
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      run: gh release upload "${TAG}" dist/manifest.yaml dist/resolved.yaml --clobber

name: signoz
description: Registry of semantic conventions for SigNoz.
schema_url: https://signoz.io/schemas/otel/0.0.1-unreleased
stability: development
dependencies:
- schema_url: https://opentelemetry.io/schemas/1.44.0
  registry_path: https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/archive/refs/tags/v1.44.0.zip[model]

groups:
- id: entity.signoz.workspace
  type: entity
  name: signoz.workspace
  stability: development
  brief: >
    A SigNoz workspace.
  attributes:
  - ref: signoz.workspace.name
    role: identifying
    requirement_level: required

- id: entity.signoz.workspace.key
  type: entity
  name: signoz.workspace.key
  stability: development
  brief: >
    A key of a SigNoz workspace.
  attributes:
  - ref: signoz.workspace.key.id
    role: identifying
    requirement_level: required

groups:
- id: registry.signoz.workspace
  type: attribute_group
  display_name: SigNoz Workspace Attributes
  brief: >
    Attributes that identify the SigNoz workspace, and the key within it, under which a piece of telemetry was ingested.
  note: |
    Set at ingestion time by the SigNoz gateway. If any of these attributes are already present in the incoming
    telemetry, the gateway overwrites them. They are therefore absent from telemetry that did not pass through the
    gateway, for example in installations that run without it.
  attributes:
  - id: signoz.workspace.key.id
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      Identifier of the key that authenticated the telemetry.
    note: |
      Useful for identifying which key the telemetry was ingested under.
    examples:
    - "019d9a99-f8f0-7e50-8bb3-995599fa1f76"
  - id: signoz.workspace.name
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      Identifier of the workspace under which the telemetry was ingested.
    note: |
      Useful for identifying which workspace the telemetry was ingested under.
    examples:
    - "acme-prod"

groups:
- id: registry.signoz.meter
  type: attribute_group
  display_name: SigNoz Meter Attributes
  brief: >
    Attributes that describe SigNoz meter metrics.
  attributes:
  - id: connector_id
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      The identifier of the meter connector instance that produced the
      metric.
    note: |
      A UUID assigned when the connector instance is created.
    examples:
    - "0b8f4a6e-2c1d-4e5f-9a7b-3c6d8e1f2a4b"
    annotations:
      signoz:
        policy_exceptions:
        - naming_convention_attr_has_namespace
        - namespace_not_vendor
  - id: signoz.io/workload
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      The SigNoz workload a Kubernetes node is dedicated to.
    note: |
      The value of the node's `signoz.io/workload` label.

      Known values: `clickhouse`, `redpanda`, `consumers`, `zookeeper`,
      `gateway`, `signoz`.
    examples:
    - "clickhouse"
    annotations:
      signoz:
        policy_exceptions:
        - naming_convention_attr_has_namespace
        - naming_convention_attr_name

groups:
- id: registry.signoz.organization
  type: attribute_group
  display_name: SigNoz Organization Attributes
  brief: >
    Attributes that identify a SigNoz organization.
  note: |
    An organization is the logical grouping of everything one SigNoz
    account holds: metaresources such as dashboards and alert rules, and
    telemetry resources such as logs, traces and metrics.
  attributes:
  - id: signoz.organization.id
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      Unique identifier of the organization.
    note: |
      The value is an opaque string: a UUID today, but the format may
      change.
    examples:
    - "58b0e1c2-3f6a-4c2e-9d3b-2f0a1b2c3d4e"

- id: registry.signoz.principal
  type: attribute_group
  display_name: SigNoz Principal Attributes
  brief: >
    Attributes that describe the principal, an authenticated user or service account.
  note: |
    The principal is also modelled as the entity `signoz.principal` (see
    `entities.yaml`).
  attributes:
  - id: signoz.principal.id
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      Unique identifier of the principal.
    note: |
      Identifies a user or a service account, as indicated by
      `signoz.principal.type`.
    examples:
    - "7c1d9e40-8a2b-4f6d-b1c3-9e5f7a0d2b4c"
  - id: signoz.principal.type
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      Kind of the principal.
    note: |
      Known values: `user` (a human user of the SigNoz platform) and
      `service_account` (a non-human principal that authenticates with an API
      key).
    examples:
    - "user"
  - id: signoz.principal.email
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      Email address of the principal.
    note: |
      > [!WARNING]
      > This attribute may contain sensitive personally identifiable
      > information (PII).
    examples:
    - "jane.doe@example.com"

groups:
- id: entity.signoz.organization
  type: entity
  name: signoz.organization
  stability: development
  brief: >
    A SigNoz organization, the logical grouping of everything one SigNoz account holds.
  note: |
    Identified by its id alone.
  attributes:
  - ref: signoz.organization.id
    role: identifying
    requirement_level: required

- id: entity.signoz.principal
  type: entity
  name: signoz.principal
  stability: development
  brief: >
    A principal of the SigNoz platform: an authenticated user or service account.
  note: |
    Identified by its id alone, which is unique across principal types; the
    type is therefore descriptive rather than part of the identity.
  attributes:
  - ref: signoz.principal.id
    role: identifying
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: signoz.principal.type
    role: descriptive
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: signoz.principal.email
    role: descriptive

groups:
- id: entity.signoz.resource
  type: entity
  name: signoz.resource
  stability: development
  brief: >
    A SigNoz platform resource: an object the platform manages, such as a dashboard, an alert rule or an ingestion key.
  note: |
    Identified by its kind and id together: ids are unique within a kind and
    organization, not across kinds. Operations on a collection, for example
    listing all resources of a kind, use the id `*` and therefore do not
    identify a single resource.
  attributes:
  - ref: signoz.resource.kind
    role: identifying
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: signoz.resource.id
    role: identifying
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: signoz.resource.object
    role: descriptive

groups:
- id: registry.signoz.audit
  type: attribute_group
  display_name: SigNoz Audit Attributes
  brief: >
    Attributes that describe an audited operation on the SigNoz platform.
  note: |
    An audit record describes who performed which operation on which
    resource, and whether it succeeded.
  attributes:
  - id: signoz.audit.verb
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      Operation the principal performed on the resource.
    note: |
      Known values: `create`, `update`, `delete`, `attach`, `detach`.

      `attach` and `detach` relate two resources and are recorded once from
      each side, with `signoz.resource.target.*` describing the other side.
    examples:
    - "update"
  - id: signoz.audit.action_category
    type:
      members:
      - id: access_control
        value: "access_control"
        stability: development
        brief: >
          A change to who may do what, such as a role assignment or a
          credential change.
      - id: configuration_changes
        value: "configuration_changes"
        stability: development
        brief: >
          A change to a metaresource or a platform setting, such as a
          dashboard or an alert rule change.
    stability: development
    brief: >
      Category of the audited operation.
    note: |
      Values are audit event categories of IEC 62443-3-3 SR 2.8, lowercased
      with words joined by underscores.
    examples:
    - "configuration_changes"
  - id: signoz.audit.outcome
    type:
      members:
      - id: success
        value: "success"
        stability: development
        brief: >
          The operation succeeded.
      - id: failure
        value: "failure"
        stability: development
        brief: >
          The operation failed.
    stability: development
    brief: >
      Outcome of the audited operation.
    note: |
      The set is complete.

      An operation served over HTTP counts as a success when the response
      status code is 2xx or 3xx. A failed operation also carries the upstream
      `exception.*` attributes describing the failure.
    examples:
    - "success"

groups:
- id: registry.signoz.gen_ai
  type: attribute_group
  display_name: SigNoz GenAI Attributes
  brief: >
    Attributes that SigNoz records for a generative AI model call.
  note: |
    The `*.cost` attributes record what a call cost, in US dollars. Each is
    named for the `gen_ai.usage.*` attribute it prices, with `.cost` appended,
    so a count and its cost share a name.
  attributes:
  - id: signoz.gen_ai.usage.tokens.cost
    type: double
    stability: development
    brief: >
      The total monetary cost of the tokens a model call used.
    note: |
      The sum of the per-class costs. Upstream has no count for all classes
      together, so this name has no `gen_ai.usage.*` counterpart.

      This value SHOULD include all charges for the tokens on the call: the
      input and output tokens, and any tokens read from or written to a cache.

      The per-class costs are disjoint and sum to this value. They do not nest
      the way the counts they are derived from do, where
      `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens` is a subset of
      `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`; tokens are priced in exactly one class.
    examples:
    - 0.00234
    - 0.4812
  - id: signoz.gen_ai.usage.input_tokens.cost
    type: double
    stability: development
    brief: >
      The monetary cost of the input tokens billed at the model's standard input rate.
    note: |
      `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` with `.cost` appended. The value SHOULD be
      included in `signoz.gen_ai.usage.tokens.cost`.

      Tokens read from or written to a provider-managed cache are billed at
      their own rates and are excluded here, even though
      `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` counts them.
    examples:
    - 0.00075
  - id: signoz.gen_ai.usage.output_tokens.cost
    type: double
    stability: development
    brief: >
      The monetary cost of the output tokens a model generated.
    note: |
      `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` with `.cost` appended. The value SHOULD be
      included in `signoz.gen_ai.usage.tokens.cost`.

      Reasoning tokens are part of the output and are priced with it.
    examples:
    - 0.00159
  - id: signoz.gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens.cost
    type: double
    stability: development
    brief: >
      The monetary cost of the input tokens served from a provider-managed cache.
    note: |
      `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens` with `.cost` appended. The value
      SHOULD be included in `signoz.gen_ai.usage.tokens.cost`.

      Providers price cache reads below their standard input rate.
    examples:
    - 0.00003
  - id: signoz.gen_ai.usage.cache_write.input_tokens.cost
    type: double
    stability: development
    brief: >
      The monetary cost of the input tokens written to a provider-managed cache.
    note: |
      `gen_ai.usage.cache_write.input_tokens` with `.cost` appended. The value
      SHOULD be included in `signoz.gen_ai.usage.tokens.cost`.

      Providers price cache writes above their standard input rate.
    examples:
    - 0.00094

groups:
- id: attributes.signoz.spanmetrics.common
  type: attribute_group

    Attributes shared by every SigNoz span metric.

    The dimensions are configurable: further span or resource attributes MAY

  - ref: service.name

      than are tracked.
  - ref: status.code
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: signoz.collector.id
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: resource_signoz.collector.id
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: service.namespace
    requirement_level: recommended
    note: |
      Set to `default` when neither the span nor its Resource carries it.
  - ref: resource_service.namespace
    requirement_level:
      conditionally_required: If the span's Resource carries `service.namespace`.
  - ref: deployment.environment
    requirement_level: recommended
    note: |
      Set to `default` when neither the span nor its Resource carries it.
  - ref: resource_deployment.environment
    requirement_level:
      conditionally_required: If the span's Resource carries `deployment.environment`.

  - ref: span.kind
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: http.status_code

  type: metric

  - ref: http.status_code

groups:
- id: attributes.signoz.meter.common
  type: attribute_group
  brief: >
    Attributes shared by every SigNoz meter metric.
  note: |
    `connector_id` is set on the instrumentation scope. Every other attribute
    is a resource attribute of the metered telemetry, recorded under its own
    key with its value as a string. These are configurable: further resource
    attributes MAY be recorded the same way, and an attribute is omitted when
    the metered telemetry does not carry it.
  attributes:
  - ref: connector_id
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: service.name
    requirement_level: recommended
  - ref: deployment.environment
    requirement_level: recommended
  - ref: host.name
    requirement_level: recommended

- id: metric.signoz.meter.log.count
  type: metric
  metric_name: signoz.meter.log.count
  stability: development
  brief: >
    The number of log records observed.
  note: |
    Each log record counts as one.
  instrument: counter
  unit: "1"
  annotations:
    signoz:
      policy_exceptions:
      - counter_unit_one
  extends: attributes.signoz.meter.common

- id: metric.signoz.meter.log.size
  type: metric
  metric_name: signoz.meter.log.size
  stability: development
  brief: >
    The size of log records observed.
  note: |
    The size of a log record is the size of its resource attributes, its
    attributes and its body. `signoz.workspace.*` attributes are not
    counted.
  instrument: counter
  unit: "By"
  extends: attributes.signoz.meter.common

- id: metric.signoz.meter.span.count
  type: metric
  metric_name: signoz.meter.span.count
  stability: development
  brief: >
    The number of spans observed.
  note: |
    Each span counts as one.
  instrument: counter
  unit: "1"
  annotations:
    signoz:
      policy_exceptions:
      - counter_unit_one
  extends: attributes.signoz.meter.common

- id: metric.signoz.meter.span.size
  type: metric
  metric_name: signoz.meter.span.size
  stability: development
  brief: >
    The size of spans observed.
  note: |
    The size of a span is the size of its fields, its resource attributes,
    its attributes, its events and its links. `signoz.workspace.*` and
    `signoz.gen_ai.*` attributes are not counted.
  instrument: counter
  unit: "By"
  extends: attributes.signoz.meter.common

- id: metric.signoz.meter.metric.datapoint.count
  type: metric
  metric_name: signoz.meter.metric.datapoint.count
  stability: development
  brief: >
    The number of metric data points observed.
  note: |
    A gauge or sum data point counts as one. A histogram data point counts
    as its number of buckets plus one for its count and one each for its
    sum, min and max when present.
    A summary data point counts as its number of quantiles plus two.
    Exponential histogram data points, and metrics whose name starts with
    `signoz` or `otelcol`, are not counted.
  instrument: counter
  unit: "1"
  annotations:
    signoz:
      policy_exceptions:
      - counter_unit_one
  extends: attributes.signoz.meter.common

- id: metric.signoz.meter.metric.datapoint.size
  type: metric
  metric_name: signoz.meter.metric.datapoint.size
  stability: development
  brief: >
    The size of metric data points observed.
  note: |
    The value is always `0`.
  instrument: counter
  unit: "By"
  extends: attributes.signoz.meter.common

- id: metric.signoz.meter.cpu.node.allocatable.usage
  type: metric
  metric_name: signoz.meter.cpu.node.allocatable.usage
  stability: development
  brief: >
    The amount of CPU allocatable on a Kubernetes node that runs SigNoz.
  note: |
    The value is in CPU cores and is recorded once per node every hour.
  instrument: gauge
  unit: "{cpu}"
  attributes:
  - ref: k8s.node.name
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: k8s.node.uid
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: signoz.io/workload
    requirement_level: required
  entity_associations:
  - k8s.node

groups:
- id: registry.signoz.resource
  type: attribute_group
  display_name: SigNoz Resource Attributes
  brief: >
    Attributes that identify a SigNoz platform resource, and the counterpart resource of a relation.
  note: |
    A resource is an object the SigNoz platform manages: a metaresource such
    as a dashboard or an alert rule, a telemetry resource such as the logs,
    traces or metrics of an organization, or a platform object such as an
    ingestion key or a license.

    The term is unrelated to the OpenTelemetry Resource. Each signal that
    carries these attributes defines whether they appear as signal attributes
    or on the OpenTelemetry Resource.

    The resource is also modelled as the entity `signoz.resource` (see
    `entities.yaml`).
  attributes:
  - id: signoz.resource.kind
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      Kind of the resource.
    note: |
      Kind values are lowercase, with words joined by hyphens.

      Known values include metaresource kinds such as `dashboard` and
      `alert-rule`; telemetry resource kinds `logs`, `traces`, `metrics`,
      `meter-metrics`, `logs-field` and `traces-field`; and platform object
      kinds such as `ingestion-key`, `ingestion-limit`, `license`,
      `subscription` and `deployment-host`. The set is not final.
    examples:
    - "ingestion-key"
  - id: signoz.resource.id
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      Unique identifier of the resource.
    note: |
      The id is unique within its kind and organization, not across kinds.
      Its format depends on the kind; most platform objects use a UUID.

      The value `*` denotes the collection of all resources of the kind and
      is used when an operation applies to the collection rather than to a
      single resource, for example a list operation.
    examples:
    - "3f8a2c14-9b7d-4e1f-a6c3-5d8e2f0b1a4c"
    - "*"
  - id: signoz.resource.object
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      Object reference of the resource in the authorization model.
    note: |
      The grammar is `<type>:organization/<organization id>/<kind>/<selector>`.
      For telemetry resources the type is `telemetryresource` and the selector
      is replaced by its SHA-256 hash truncated to 16 hexadecimal characters.
    examples:
    - "telemetryresource:organization/58b0e1c2-3f6a-4c2e-9d3b-2f0a1b2c3d4e/logs/2c26b46b68ffc68f"
  - id: signoz.resource.target.kind
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      Kind of the counterpart resource in a relation.
    note: |
      Set on operations that relate two resources, for example attach and
      detach: `attach dashboard D to alert rule R` records R as the target.
      Relations emit one event per side; in each event the
      `signoz.resource.*` attributes describe the side the event is recorded
      from and the `signoz.resource.target.*` attributes the other side.

      Takes the same values as `signoz.resource.kind`.
    examples:
    - "dashboard"
  - id: signoz.resource.target.id
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      Unique identifier of the counterpart resource in a relation.
    note: |
      Set on operations that relate two resources, for example attach and
      detach. Follows the same rules as `signoz.resource.id`.
    examples:
    - "7c1d9e40-8a2b-4f6d-b1c3-9e5f7a0d2b4c"
  - id: signoz.resource.target.object
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      Object reference of the counterpart resource in a relation.
    note: |
      Set on operations that relate two resources, for example attach and
      detach. Follows the same grammar as `signoz.resource.object`.
    examples:
    - "telemetryresource:organization/58b0e1c2-3f6a-4c2e-9d3b-2f0a1b2c3d4e/traces/9f86d081884c7d65"

groups:
- id: attributes.signoz.audit.common
  type: attribute_group
  brief: >
    Attributes shared by every SigNoz audit event.
  note: |
    `signoz.resource.*` are set on the OpenTelemetry Resource; every other
    attribute is set on the log record.

    The body, when set, is a human-readable sentence describing the
    operation, including the principal's email address. It carries no
    information that is not also recorded as an attribute.

    > [!WARNING]
    > The body contains personally identifiable information (PII).
  attributes:
  - ref: signoz.audit.verb
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: signoz.audit.action_category
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: signoz.audit.outcome
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: signoz.organization.id
    requirement_level: required
    brief: >
      Organization that owns the resource the operation was performed on.
  - ref: signoz.resource.kind
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: signoz.resource.id
    requirement_level: required
    note: |
      Set to `*` when the operation applies to the collection of all
      resources of the kind rather than to a single resource.
  - ref: signoz.resource.object
    requirement_level: recommended
  - ref: signoz.principal.id
    requirement_level:
      conditionally_required: If the request was authenticated.
    note: |
      The user or the service account that performed the operation.
  - ref: signoz.principal.type
    requirement_level:
      conditionally_required: If the request was authenticated.
  - ref: signoz.principal.email
    requirement_level: recommended
    note: |
      Set for user principals; service accounts have no email address.

      > [!WARNING]
      > This attribute contains personally identifiable information (PII).
  - ref: signoz.workspace.key.id
    requirement_level:
      conditionally_required: If `signoz.resource.kind` is `ingestion-key`.
    note: |
      The ingestion key the audited resource is or belongs to. When
      `signoz.resource.kind` is `ingestion-key` the value equals
      `signoz.resource.id`; it SHOULD also be set when the kind is
      `ingestion-limit`.
  - ref: exception.type
    requirement_level:
      conditionally_required: If `signoz.audit.outcome` is `failure`.
    note: |
      The class of the failure. Values are the error types the platform
      raises: `invalid-input`, `not-found`, `already-exists`,
      `unauthenticated`, `forbidden`, `unsupported`, `canceled`, `timeout`,
      `license-unavailable`, `too-many-requests` and `internal`.
  - ref: exception.message
    requirement_level: opt_in
    note: |
      > [!WARNING]
      > Exception messages may contain user-supplied data.
  - ref: exception.stacktrace
    requirement_level: opt_in
  - ref: http.request.method
    requirement_level:
      conditionally_required: If the operation was served over HTTP.
  - ref: http.route
    requirement_level:
      conditionally_required: If the operation was served over HTTP and a route matched.
  - ref: http.response.status_code
    requirement_level:
      conditionally_required: If the operation was served over HTTP.
  - ref: url.scheme
    requirement_level: recommended
  - ref: url.path
    requirement_level: opt_in
    note: |
      > [!WARNING]
      > Path segments contain resource identifiers, including those of
      > resources the principal was not allowed to reach.
  - ref: client.address
    requirement_level: recommended
    note: |
      The address the request came from, without the port. The port is
      `client.port`.
  - ref: client.port
    requirement_level: recommended
  - ref: user_agent.original
    requirement_level: recommended
  - ref: network.protocol.name
    requirement_level: recommended
  - ref: network.protocol.version
    requirement_level: recommended

- id: event.signoz.audit.create
  type: event
  name: signoz.audit.create
  stability: development
  extends: attributes.signoz.audit.common
  brief: >
    Records the creation of a SigNoz resource.
  note: |
    Recorded once per creation, after the operation has completed. The
    timestamp is the time of the operation.

    Severity SHOULD be `INFO` (9) when `signoz.audit.outcome` is `success`
    and `ERROR` (17) when it is `failure`.
  entity_associations:
  - signoz.resource

- id: event.signoz.audit.update
  type: event
  name: signoz.audit.update
  stability: development
  extends: attributes.signoz.audit.common
  brief: >
    Records the modification of a SigNoz resource.
  note: |
    Recorded once per modification, after the operation has completed. The
    timestamp is the time of the operation.

    Severity SHOULD be `INFO` (9) when `signoz.audit.outcome` is `success`
    and `ERROR` (17) when it is `failure`.
  entity_associations:
  - signoz.resource

- id: event.signoz.audit.delete
  type: event
  name: signoz.audit.delete
  stability: development
  extends: attributes.signoz.audit.common
  brief: >
    Records the deletion of a SigNoz resource.
  note: |
    Recorded once per deletion, after the operation has completed. The
    timestamp is the time of the operation.

    Severity SHOULD be `INFO` (9) when `signoz.audit.outcome` is `success`
    and `ERROR` (17) when it is `failure`.
  entity_associations:
  - signoz.resource

- id: event.signoz.audit.attach
  type: event
  name: signoz.audit.attach
  stability: development
  extends: attributes.signoz.audit.common
  brief: >
    Records the attachment of one SigNoz resource to another.
  note: |
    Recorded twice per attachment, once from each side of the relation,
    after the operation has completed. For `attach dashboard D to alert rule
    R`, one record describes D with `signoz.resource.*` and R with
    `signoz.resource.target.*`, and the other record swaps them. The
    timestamp is the time of the operation.

    Severity SHOULD be `INFO` (9) when `signoz.audit.outcome` is `success`
    and `ERROR` (17) when it is `failure`.
  attributes:
  - ref: signoz.resource.target.kind
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: signoz.resource.target.id
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: signoz.resource.target.object
    requirement_level: recommended
  entity_associations:
  - signoz.resource

- id: event.signoz.audit.detach
  type: event
  name: signoz.audit.detach
  stability: development
  extends: attributes.signoz.audit.common
  brief: >
    Records the detachment of one SigNoz resource from another.
  note: |
    Recorded twice per detachment, once from each side of the relation,
    after the operation has completed. For `detach dashboard D from alert
    rule R`, one record describes D with `signoz.resource.*` and R with
    `signoz.resource.target.*`, and the other record swaps them. The
    timestamp is the time of the operation.

    Severity SHOULD be `INFO` (9) when `signoz.audit.outcome` is `success`
    and `ERROR` (17) when it is `failure`.
  attributes:
  - ref: signoz.resource.target.kind
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: signoz.resource.target.id
    requirement_level: required
  - ref: signoz.resource.target.object
    requirement_level: recommended
  entity_associations:
  - signoz.resource

groups:
- id: registry.signoz.spanmetrics
  type: attribute_group
  display_name: SigNoz Span Metrics Attributes
  brief: >
    Attributes that describe SigNoz span metrics.
  attributes:
  - id: signoz.collector.id
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      The identifier of the collector instance that produced the metric.
    note: |
      The collector's `service.instance.id`, or a UUID assigned when the
      collector starts if it has none.
    examples:
    - "6f1c2b7e-4d3a-4b8f-9e21-5a0c7d9b3e14"
  - id: resource_signoz.collector.id
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      A copy of `signoz.collector.id`.
    examples:
    - "6f1c2b7e-4d3a-4b8f-9e21-5a0c7d9b3e14"
    annotations:
      signoz:
        policy_exceptions:
        - namespace_not_vendor
  - id: operation
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      The name of the aggregated spans.
    note: |
      Set to `overflow_operation` when the service has more distinct span
      names than are tracked.
    examples:
    - "GET /api/v1/orders/{id}"
    - "overflow_operation"
    annotations:
      signoz:
        policy_exceptions:
        - naming_convention_attr_has_namespace
        - namespace_not_vendor
  - id: span.kind
    type:
      members:
      - id: unspecified
        value: "SPAN_KIND_UNSPECIFIED"
        stability: development
        brief: >
          The span kind is unspecified.
      - id: internal
        value: "SPAN_KIND_INTERNAL"
        stability: development
        brief: >
          An internal operation.
      - id: server
        value: "SPAN_KIND_SERVER"
        stability: development
        brief: >
          The server side of a remote call.
      - id: client
        value: "SPAN_KIND_CLIENT"
        stability: development
        brief: >
          The client side of a remote call.
      - id: producer
        value: "SPAN_KIND_PRODUCER"
        stability: development
        brief: >
          The producer of an asynchronous message.
      - id: consumer
        value: "SPAN_KIND_CONSUMER"
        stability: development
        brief: >
          The consumer of an asynchronous message.
    stability: development
    brief: >
      The kind of the aggregated spans.
    examples:
    - "SPAN_KIND_SERVER"
    annotations:
      signoz:
        policy_exceptions:
        - namespace_not_vendor
  - id: status.code
    type:
      members:
      - id: unset
        value: "STATUS_CODE_UNSET"
        stability: development
        brief: >
          The span status is unset.
      - id: ok
        value: "STATUS_CODE_OK"
        stability: development
        brief: >
          The span completed successfully.
      - id: error
        value: "STATUS_CODE_ERROR"
        stability: development
        brief: >
          The span completed with an error.
    stability: development
    brief: >
      The status code of the aggregated spans.
    examples:
    - "STATUS_CODE_ERROR"
    annotations:
      signoz:
        policy_exceptions:
        - namespace_not_vendor
  - id: address
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      The remote endpoint of an external call.
    note: |
      `<rpc.service>/<rpc.method>` for RPC calls, otherwise the remote host
      as `host` or `host:port`, or the span's `peer.service`.
    examples:
    - "payments.internal:8443"
    - "oteldemo.CartService/GetCart"
    annotations:
      signoz:
        policy_exceptions:
        - naming_convention_attr_has_namespace
        - namespace_not_vendor
  - id: resource_service.namespace
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      The value of `service.namespace` on the span's Resource.
    examples:
    - "shop"
    annotations:
      signoz:
        policy_exceptions:
        - namespace_not_vendor
  - id: resource_deployment.environment
    type: string
    stability: development
    brief: >
      The value of `deployment.environment` on the span's Resource.
    examples:
    - "production"
    annotations:
      signoz:
        policy_exceptions:
        - namespace_not_vendor

SigNoz Semantic Conventions

The names, types and meanings of the telemetry SigNoz emits and reads.

## Overview The conventions are an [OpenTelemetry Weaver](https://github.com/open-telemetry/weaver) registry built on the [OpenTelemetry semantic conventions](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions). The YAML definitions are in [`model/`](model), one folder per area, and the generated [docs](docs/README.md) list every attribute, metric, event and entity. ## Using the conventions To build on these conventions in your own Weaver registry, depend on a [release](https://github.com/SigNoz/signoz-semantic-conventions/releases) in your `manifest.yaml`, then reference the attributes by key: ```yaml dependencies: - schema_url: https://signoz.io/schemas/otel/ registry_path: https://github.com/SigNoz/signoz-semantic-conventions/archive/refs/tags/v.zip[model] ``` Each release also carries the resolved registry (`resolved.yaml`) for tools that read it directly. [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md) describes how versions and releases work. ## Contributing Open an [issue](https://github.com/SigNoz/signoz-semantic-conventions/issues) or a pull request, ask in `#contributing` on the [SigNoz Slack](https://signoz.io/slack), or share ideas in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/SigNoz/signoz/discussions). Changes are checked with [weaver](https://github.com/open-telemetry/weaver/releases) and [yamllint](https://github.com/adrienverge/yamllint): run `make yaml-lint`, `make weaver-check` and `make weaver-docs`, and commit the regenerated `docs/` with your change. .PHONY: weaver-check
weaver-check: ## Runs weaver check with the rego policies.
	@dups="$$(grep -rhE '^- id: |^  metric_name: ' model | sed -E 's/ *#.*//; s/["'"'"']//g; s/ +$$//' | sort | uniq -d)"; \
		if [ -n "$$dups" ]; then echo "Defined more than once in model/:"; echo "$$dups"; exit 1; fi
	@weaver registry check --registry model/ --policy policies/before_resolution
	@weaver registry check --registry model/ --v2 --policy policies/after_resolution \
		$(foreach policy,$(WEAVER_PACKAGES_POLICIES),--policy '$(WEAVER_PACKAGES)[$(policy)]')

.PHONY: weaver-docs
weaver-docs: ## Generate docs/ from the registry.
	@rm -rf docs
	@weaver registry generate --registry model/ --v2 --quiet markdown docs

# Model files

## YAML

- Weaver's v1 `groups:` format only; never `file_format: definition/2`.
- `brief:` is always a `>` block and `note:` a `|` block. One blank line between groups.
- Attributes are defined only in `registry.*` attribute groups; every other group references them with `- ref:`.
- A `ref` never sets `stability` or `deprecated`; weaver silently applies them to that signal. It may refine only `brief`, `note`, `examples`, `tag`, `annotations`, `requirement_level`, `sampling_relevant` and (entities) `role`. An inline `ref` beats one inherited through `extends`; along an `extends` chain the nearest wins.
- Events have no `body:`; describe any display-message body in the `note`.
- Examples: `string[]` takes a list of lists (`- - "a"`); template examples are values, not `key=value`.
- `imports:` match spans and attribute groups by group id (`span.http.client`, `client`), metrics and events by name, entities by type.

## Names

- SigNoz names start with `signoz.`. An upstream key is referenced, never redefined, and nothing new goes under an upstream namespace such as `http.` or `db.`.
- Two attributes, two metrics or two events never share a name.

## Changing what exists

- Never delete or rename an emitted name in place: move the old definition to `model/<area>/deprecated/` with a structured `deprecated:` block.
- A stable convention never changes an attribute's type, an enum member's value (and never loses a member), a metric's unit or instrument, a span's kind or an entity's identity. Stable attributes are never dropped from stable signals, and a stable metric only gains `opt_in` attributes.
- A rename that only swaps `_` and `.` (`rule_id` to `rule.id`) gives both names one code constant; set `annotations.code_generation.exclude: true` on the old one.

## Exceptions

- Only for names already emitted; anything new gets a name that passes.
- List the rule id under `annotations.signoz.policy_exceptions` for our rules, `annotations.stability.policy_exceptions` (finding id minus `stability_`) or `annotations.naming_conventions.policy_exceptions` (only `metric_namespace_collision`) for upstream's.

## Briefs and notes

- A `brief` is one noun phrase, usually starting with "The".
- Say what a thing is, never how it is produced, stored or queried, or why it was designed that way.
- Group notes are one or two lines. Don't restate the YAML: requirement level, `extends`, event name or type.
- A possibly sensitive value gets a `> [!WARNING]` note saying what is sensitive, with no operating advice.

## Before committing

Run `make yaml-lint weaver-check weaver-docs` and commit the regenerated `docs/`.

package after_resolution

import rego.v1

# Every entity has at least one identifying attribute. Upstream's stability
# package checks this for stable entities only.

deny contains finding if {
	some entity in input.registry.entities
	count(object.get(entity, "identity", [])) == 0
	finding := signoz_signal_finding({"type": "entity", "name": entity.type}, "entity_no_identifying", sprintf(
		"Entity '%s' has no identifying attribute.",
		[entity.type],
	))
}
